business_problem: AETA needed to improve the accuracy and operational readiness of its earthquake-prediction system so governments could act on its forecasts with more confidence.
solution_summary: AETA and Capgemini's AIE Shenzhen advanced earthquake prediction by combining a sensor network, competition platform, and neural modeling workflow into one AI pipeline. AETA's three-part sensing systems collect electromagnetic and geo-acoustic data across high-seismic regions, and a competition system ingests weekly forecasts plus real outcomes so models can be compared against ground truth. The winning WALKTREE approach uses a deep neural network that first narrows likely regions through longitude and latitude prediction, then classifies expected earthquake magnitude; a lightweight network consumes maximum, minimum, and average sensor values to generate the final forecast. Alongside model improvement, AETA hardened the sensors to reduce maintenance effort, turning the project from raw data collection into a repeatable prediction workflow that can support public-warning, infrastructure, and emergency-planning decisions.

solution_components.role: Collect electromagnetic and geo-acoustic signals from seismic regions before, during, and after earthquakes.

solution_components.name: competition system
solution_components.role: Accepts weekly forecasts and real earthquake data so prediction approaches can be evaluated against outcomes.

solution_components.name: WALKTREE prediction model
solution_components.role: Uses a two-step deep-neural-network approach to forecast earthquake location and magnitude more accurately.

data_flow: Sensor systems gather electromagnetic and geo-acoustic data from target regions and feed it into the competition system alongside observed earthquake outcomes. The WALKTREE model trains on those inputs, predicts location and magnitude, and returns forecast results that can support evacuation, infrastructure, and emergency-response planning.

business_outcome: AETA significantly improved prediction accuracy, reduced sensor-maintenance effort, and established a repeatable AI workflow it can keep refining for broader public-warning use.
